scope: Isolated S1 backend loss. An experimental probe unwinds the constellation thread with live views and pending callbacks. The embedder detects the closed constellation channel, revokes every view before terminal callbacks, closes admission, and finishes shutdown locally. These cases run in a separate engine process in both modes. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.

review_fixes: Corrected the document scope guide: the interruption evidence preserves the first thirty-eight-case checkpoint, not the thirty-nine-case process checkpoint.
source_audit: ConstellationProxy marks disconnection only after a failed embedder send, so Servo reported LostConnectionWithBackend only after the host sent more work.
JavaScriptEvaluator::evaluate inserted a callback even when its send failed. No reply or revocation could reach that callback.
Pending callbacks and host scope had no revocation path after constellation loss.
ServoInner::drop spins until FinishedShuttingDown, which only the constellation's ShutdownComplete message sets. The destructor could not return after constellation loss.

The constellation owns the only ConstellationToEmbedderMsg sender, so that channel closes when the constellation thread ends. Crossbeam reports closure only after the embedder drains earlier messages.

configuration.failure_trigger: A script-thread barrier holds eight scoped and legacy requests for one view. The host then sends an experimental message that panics on the constellation thread. The constellation forwards the eight requests before it reads that message. The host sends no further work until cleanup.
configuration.runner_cleanup: Every case has its own process group. The runner kills remaining group members after normal completion or a deadline.

backend_timings.note: Cleanup is measured from the crash request. The panic hook logs immediately, so the delay occurs during the constellation unwind. The debug linker reports that unwind tables exceed its compact-unwind limit. The cause of the delay is not established. These are not latency measurements.

local_validation.patch_reproduction: The edited patch applies to the published packages with patch -F 0. Its patched sources are byte-identical to the edited source tree.
local_validation.patch_editing: Unchanged files keep their committed hunks. New constellation lines were spliced into the committed hunks, and only the affected hunk headers were recounted.
local_validation.binary_isolation: Each run used a private copy of its binary, so concurrent builds in the shared target directory could not replace it.
local_validation.binary_restoration: Rebuilt the final preparation after the negative controls. target/debug/bulwark-experiment-e4 matches the SHA-256 of both passing final reports.
local_validation.product_changes: None. Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, product crates, and installed natives are unchanged.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
The backend fixture covers an unwind of the constellation thread only. A hung constellation, a process abort, and loss of other engine threads remain untested.
The constellation ignores panic reports without an event-loop identity. Failures of threads without that identity remain untested.
The fixture does not check content-process exit after backend loss. The runner stops any remaining process.
A request between the loss and its detection stays pending until the next event-loop spin.
Failures before document construction, shared-process views, normal teardown races, kills outside a barrier, and remaining replacement paths remain open.
The host allocation counter is not a production registry or handle revocation mechanism.
Upstream review must settle cancellation, interruption, lifeline recovery, backend loss, and callback/delegate unwind policy before integration.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
